newsitem.title: GERMANY: Merck gets two-mth exclusive licence in US.
newsitem.headline: Merck gets two-mth exclusive licence in US.

text.p: German drugs group Merck AG said on Friday its Toronto-based unit Genpharm on June 17 received a temporary registration from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to market a generic version of the active agent Ranitidin used in the stomach ulcer drug Zantac.
Merck said in a statement the decision means Genpharm will be the sole supplier of the drug in the U.S. until August 29.
Patent protection for Zantac ends in the U.S. on July 25.
"Due to series of complicated factors it is not possible to predict what impact, if any, the FDA decision will have on the sales and profit of the Merck group," Merck said in a statement.
But a spokeswoman for the company said the two months during which Merck would be able to market Ranitidin exclusively gave the company a "giant lead" over its competitors in the market for the drug.
"Speed is very important in this market," the spokeswoman said.
